title: Differentiating powers of x (the power rule)
keyIdea: To differentiate xⁿ, multiply by the power and then take one off the power: xⁿ becomes nxⁿ⁻¹.

kid: First principles always works, but it is slow. There is a short cut called the power rule. Multiply by the power, then take one off the power.
So x² becomes 2x, x³ becomes 3x², and x⁵ becomes 5x⁴. A plain x is x¹, so it becomes 1. A number on its own, like 7, has gradient 0.
adult: The power rule works for any power, including negative and fractional ones. Rewrite first: 1/x = x⁻¹, so its derivative is −x⁻², which is −1/x².
Likewise √x is x to the power ½, which gives ½ × x to the power −½, or 1/(2√x). That's why the laws of indices (exponents) matter here. Write each term as a power of x before you use the rule.

familyTip: Make flashcards: a power of x on one side, its derivative on the other. Test each other.

practice.hint: Multiply by the power, then take one off.

practice.prompt: y = {a}x². Find the gradient at x = {c}.
practice.explain: dy/dx = {=2*a}x, so at x = {c} it is {=2*a*c}.
1/x = x⁻¹. Multiply by −1 and take one off the power: −x⁻². A common slip is to go from −1 to 0 instead of −2.

pool.hint: Multiply by 3, take one off the power.
√x is x to the power ½.
pool.explain: Multiply by ½ and take one off the power to get −½: ½ × x to the power −½ = 1/(2√x).
1 × x⁰ = 1. The line y = x has gradient 1.

pool.prompt: Jo differentiates x⁻³ and gets −3x⁻². What went wrong?
choices: One less than −3 is −4, so it should be −3x⁻⁴
